title: Rank-one local calculation
statement:
In the finite-torsion setting of [def-pur-conventions], let $A=A_{E,n}$ for any $n\geq1$, and choose an integer $N\geq1$ such that $\ell^N A=0$. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point of a $k$-scheme, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and put
$$
X=\mathbf A^1_\Omega=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[t],\qquad
Z=V(t)\subset X,\qquad U=X\setminus Z=\mathbf G_{m,\Omega}.
$$
Thus $Z$ is the fibre of the zero section of $\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$. On the small etale site set
$$
A(1)=\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}\underline A.
$$
Use cohomology with supports as in [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Let $\delta_N$ be the boundary of the Kummer sequence [def-sc-kummer-sequence], and let $\kappa_A(u)\in H^1(U,A(1))$ be the image of $\delta_N(u)$ under the coefficient map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Then the support boundary of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] is an isomorphism
$$
\partial:H^1(U,A(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2_Z(X,A(1)),
$$
and there is a unique $A$-linear isomorphism
$$
\rho:H^2_Z(X,A(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}A,\qquad
\rho\bigl(\partial\kappa_A(t)\bigr)=1.
$$
In particular $H^q_Z(X,A(1))=0$ for every $q\geq0$ with $q\neq2$. The composite $\rho\partial$ is the residue homomorphism: for every global unit $u=c t^r$ on $U$, with $c\in\Omega^\times$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$,
$$
\rho\bigl(\partial\kappa_A(u)\bigr)=r\cdot1_A=\operatorname{ord}_0(u)\cdot1_A.
$$
Here $\operatorname{ord}_0$ is the exponent of $t$ in a nonzero rational function at $0$, so $t$ has order $1$ and every unit of $\Omega[t]_{(t)}$ has order $0$. The normalization is independent of a primitive root of unity; such a choice, provided by [lem-sc-primitive-root] and [def-sc-mu-trivialization], is used only to identify the degree-zero groups with $A$. The same result holds on the small pro-etale site for the inverse-image coefficient sheaf, under [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison].

proof.text: The finite coefficient ring is finite, and ell is invertible in Omega by the characteristic of the finite ground field. Map its ell^N unit into global sections and use the actual pure-tensor root coefficient map z |-> 1 tensor z of def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class. Apply lem-pur-rank-one-finite-kummer-cohomology to obtain the coordinate basis tau, the ordinary higher vanishings and invertible degree-zero restriction. The adopted source proves finite-abelian coefficient cohomology directly; no free coefficient hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply lem-pur-rank-one-classical-support-comparison to get the ordinary comparison in all degrees and boundaries normalized on every injective resolution. On an injective resolution, the support short complex is short exact. Its snake boundary in degrees 1,2 is an isomorphism because affine-line cohomology in both degrees vanishes. The degree-zero restriction is an isomorphism, so support degrees zero and one vanish by exactness; all higher degrees other than two vanish between the ordinary vanishing groups.

proof.text: The ordinary comparisons transfer the ordinary higher vanishings to the pro-etale site. Naturality of the underived comparison unit transfers invertibility of degree-zero restriction. The same short-complex argument makes the normalized pro-etale boundary invertible and kills its other support degrees. Thus cZ = delta_et inverse followed by cU and delta_pro is an isomorphism satisfying the boundary square; since the boundaries are invertible this square uniquely determines cZ.

proof.text: Let e = tau followed by delta_et and rho_et = e inverse. Define rho_pro = cZ inverse followed by rho_et. Their normalization follows from tau(1)=kappa(t) and inverse identities. The comparison identity is immediate. For uniqueness, precompose a candidate with e (or e followed by cZ); A-linear maps out of A are determined by the value at 1. None of these constructions uses a primitive root.

proof.text: A polynomial nonzero at zero is outside the ideal (X), so its X-adic integer valuation is one. The quotient formula gives valuation one for a/b with both evaluations nonzero. The valuation of X is exp(-1), that of a nonzero constant is one, and multiplicativity for integer powers gives valuation(c X^r)=exp(-r). This fixes ord_0(t)=1 and order zero for local units.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, let $\bar y\to Y$ be a
geometric point of $Y$ with
algebraically closed field $\Omega$, put
$Z=s(\bar y)\subset\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}=\mathbf A^1_k\times_k\Omega$, and
let $A(1)$ be the finite-level twist
$A(1)=\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$ on the
smooth separated curve $\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}$
over $\Omega$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
H^2_Z\bigl(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},A(1)\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }A,
$$

under which the boundary of the
Kummer class of the coordinate $t$
corresponds to $1\in A$; equivalently, the boundary map of the
support long exact sequence

$$
\partial:\ H^1\bigl(\mathbf G_{m,\bar y},A(1)\bigr)
\longrightarrow H^2_Z\bigl(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},A(1)\bigr)
$$

is the *residue* homomorphism and its value on $\kappa(t)$ is
the residue $1$, given by the normalization
$\operatorname{ord}_0(t)=1$ (the order of a unit of the completed
local ring at the origin is the exponent of $t$, so the boundary
of the Kummer class of the coordinate is the class of the orbit
$t\cdot(\mathbf G_m^\wedge)^{(N)}$); all other supported cohomology
groups of $A(1)$ vanish:

$$
H^q_Z(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},A(1))=0\qquad(q\neq2).
$$

The statements are those of the etale site, transported to the pro-etale
site by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], the coefficients being
finite-torsion. (The identification of the $H^0$-terms and of
$A(1)_{\bar y}\cong A$ uses a primitive $\ell^N$-th root of unity in
$\Omega$, in the sense of [def-sc-mu-trivialization], and
[lem-sc-primitive-root] for its existence.)

proof.text:
Write $X=\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}$, $U=\mathbf G_{m,\bar y}$, and apply
the long exact sequence for cohomology with support
[thm-pur-with-support-exactness] to the pair $(X,Z)$:

$$
\begin{array}{l}
0\to H^0_Z(X,A(1))\to H^0(X,A(1))\to H^0(U,A(1))\to H^1_Z(X,A(1))\\
\hphantom{0\to{}}
\to H^1(X,A(1))\to H^1(U,A(1))\to H^2_Z(X,A(1))\to H^2(X,A(1))\\
\hphantom{0\to{}}
\to H^2(U,A(1))\to H^3_Z(X,A(1))\to H^3(X,A(1))\to\cdots.
\end{array}
$$

By [thm-pur-kummer-affine-line] (with the field $\Omega$),
$H^q(X,A(1))=0$ for $q>0$,
$H^0(X,A(1))=H^0(U,A(1))=A$, and the groups on $U$ vanish except
$H^1(U,A(1))=A$, generated by the Kummer class of $t$. The
restriction map $H^0(X,A(1))\to H^0(U,A(1))$ is the identity under the
identical identification of both groups with $A$ (the sheaf $A(1)$ is
locally constant, i.e. constant after the trivialization of
[def-sc-mu-trivialization], and both schemes are connected), so the
sequence reads

$$
0\to H^0_Z(X,A(1))\to A\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }A\to H^1_Z(X,A(1))\to
0\to A\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^2_Z(X,A(1))\to 0\to 0\to\cdots.
$$

Exactness gives $H^0_Z=0$, $H^1_Z=0$, and

$$
H^2_Z(X,A(1))\cong A,
$$

the isomorphism sending the boundary of the Kummer class of $t$ to the
generator $1\in A$. Explicitly, the boundary of the support sequence is
the residue map, and its value on the Kummer class is the valuation at
the origin: under the identification
$H^1(U,A(1))\cong A$ generated by $\kappa(t)$ and
$H^2_Z(X,A(1))\cong A$, the isomorphism of the statement is
$\kappa(t)\mapsto\operatorname{ord}_0(t)=1$, i.e. the exponential of
the valuation of the completing local ring
$\mathcal O_{X,Z}^{\wedge}\cong\Omega[[t]]$, whose unit
$t$ has order one. The displayed identifications fix the
normalization without a choice of splitting (the classes of the
coordinate torsor and its boundary are the same as the classes of the
global coordinate, by the torsor form of the Kummer class of
[def-pur-affine-line-datum]). The groups $H^q_Z$ vanish for
$q>2$ since they
sit between the vanishing $H^{q-1}(U,A(1))$ and $H^q(X,A(1))$. The
pro-etale form is the comparison [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] of
the proper-base-change chapter.
